translations.idiomatic: After Liucheng Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.

sentences.zh: 後石季龍征遼，皝親將三軍略令支以北，遼議欲追之，翰知皝躬自總戎，戰必克勝，乃謂遼曰：「今石氏向至，方對大故，不宜復以小小為事。

translations.literal: Later Shi Jilong campaigned against Liao; Huang personally led the three armies raiding north of Lingzhi; Liao debated wishing to pursue him; Han knew Huang personally commanded the army, battle must seize victory; thereupon said to Liao: “Now the Shi clan is about to arrive, just facing great enemy; ought not again to take small matters as affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Shi Hu campaigned against Duan Liao and Murong Huang personally led an army to raid north of Lingzhi, Duan Liao debated pursuit. Knowing Huang commanded in person and must win, Murong Han told Duan Liao, "Now the Shi are about to arrive and you face a great enemy; you should not again take up small matters.

sentences.zh: 燕王自來，士馬精銳。

translations.literal: The King of Yan has come in person; soldiers and horses are picked and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang’s host is elite.

sentences.zh: 兵者凶器，戰有危慮，若其失利，何以南禦乎！」

translations.literal: Weapons are ill-omened tools; battle has perilous anxiety; if it misses advantage, how to defend the south!”
translations.idiomatic: War is peril—if you lose here, how will you hold the south?”

sentences.zh: 蘭怒曰：「吾前聽卿誑說，致成今患，不復入卿計中矣。」

translations.literal: Lan angrily said: “Formerly I listened to your deceitful talk, caused to complete today’s disaster; I do not again enter your schemes.”
translations.idiomatic: Duan Lan snapped, “Your last ‘advice’ ruined me—I will not heed you again.”

sentences.zh: 乃率眾追皝，蘭果大敗。

translations.literal: Thereupon led host to pursue Huang; Lan was indeed greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He chased Huang and was crushed.

sentences.zh: 翰雖處仇國，因事立忠，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Although Han dwelt in an enemy state, by events established loyalty—all was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Even in exile Murong Han worked secretly for Yan’s good.

sentences.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。

translations.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Liao fell he fled north to Yuwen Gui.

sentences.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。

translations.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Gui sent a hundred picked riders after him.

sentences.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。

translations.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.

sentences.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。

translations.literal: My bow and arrows, you lot fully know; do not force each other, self-seeking death.
translations.idiomatic: You know my archery—do not force a fight.

sentences.zh: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。

translations.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
translations.idiomatic: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.

sentences.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；

translations.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if I shoot the center, you then conveniently turn back;
translations.idiomatic: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I ring it, withdraw;

sentences.zh: 不中者，可來前也。」

translations.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”
translations.idiomatic: if I miss, come on.”

sentences.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。

translations.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.

sentences.zh: 既至，皝甚加恩禮，

translations.literal: Having arrived, Huang greatly added favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Huang welcomed him with rich honors.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，從皝討宇文歸，臨陣為流矢所中，臥病積時。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, Huang followed to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle was struck by a stray arrow; lay ill accumulated time.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan, he joined the war on Yuwen Gui, took a stray shaft, and lay long ill.

sentences.zh: 後疾漸愈，於其家中騎馬自試，或有人告翰私習騎，疑為非常。

translations.literal: Later illness gradually improved; at his home mounted horse to test himself; someone reported Han privately practiced riding, suspected as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: When he tried riding at home, informers called it sedition.

sentences.zh: 皝素忌之，遂賜死焉。

translations.literal: Huang plain envied him; thereupon granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, who had always feared him, sent him poison.

sentences.zh: 翰臨死謂使者曰：「翰懷疑外奔，罪不容誅，不能以骸骨委賊庭，故歸罪有司。

translations.literal: Han nearing death told the envoy: “Han harbored suspicion and fled abroad; crime does not permit execution; could not cast bones in the bandit court; therefore returned guilt to the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han told the messenger, “I fled in fear and deserved death, yet I would not die in a foreign hall, so I came home to face judgment.

sentences.zh: 天慈曲湣，不肆之市朝，今日之死，翰之生也。

translations.literal: Heaven’s kindness bent pity, did not display me in the marketplace; today’s death is Han’s life.
translations.idiomatic: The king spared me a public execution—this death is mercy.

sentences.zh: 但逆胡跨據神州，中原未靖，翰常克心自誓，志吞醜虜，上成先王遺旨，下謝山海之責。

translations.literal: But the rebellious Hu stride occupying the divine continent; the central plain is not yet quieted; Han constantly set heart to swear, intent to swallow the ugly bandits, above to complete the late king’s leftover command, below to apologize for the duty to mountains and seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Hu still hold the Central Plain; I had hoped to cleanse them for Murong Hui’s sake.

sentences.zh: 不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何！」

translations.literal: Did not expect this heart not to succeed; dying there is surplus regret—fate it—what to do!”
translations.idiomatic: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”

sentences.zh: 仰藥而死。

translations.literal: Raised poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank the poison and died.

sentences.zh: 陽裕

translations.literal: Yang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu.

sentences.zh: 陽裕，字士倫，右北平無終人也。

translations.literal: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, was a man of Wuzhong in Right Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu, courtesy name Shilun, came from Wuzhong in right Beiping.

sentences.zh: 少孤，兄弟皆早亡，單煢獨立，雖宗族無能識者，惟叔父耽幼而奇之，曰：「此兒非惟吾門之標秀，乃佐時之良器也。」

translations.literal: In youth orphaned, brothers all died early, alone and solitary; although the lineage group none could recognize him, only uncle Dan in youth wondered at him, saying: “This child is not only our gate’s outstanding show, but an instrument to aid the age.”
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, with brothers dead early, he stood alone; few in the clan knew him, but his uncle Dan marveled at him even in youth and said, "This child is not only our clan's outstanding ornament but an instrument to serve the age."

sentences.zh: 刺史和演辟為主簿。

translations.literal: The governor He Yan summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Governor He Yan made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 王浚領州，轉治中從事，忌而不能任。

translations.literal: Wang Jun held the province, transferred to aide in the bureau of administration, envied yet could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Jun he rose to administration aide but was distrusted.

sentences.zh: 石勒既克薊城，問棗嵩曰：「幽州人士，誰最可者？」

translations.literal: After Shi Le took Ji city, asked Zao Song, saying: “Youzhou gentlemen, who is most worthy?”
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Le took Jicheng he asked Zao Song, "Among the gentlemen of Youzhou, who is most worthy?"

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「燕國劉翰，德素長者。

translations.literal: Song said: “Yan state’s Liu Han, virtue is plain elder.
translations.idiomatic: Zao Song said, "Liu Han of Yan, whose virtue is that of a plain elder.

sentences.zh: 北平陽裕，幹事之才。」

translations.literal: Beiping’s Yang Yu, talent for handling affairs.”
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu of Beiping for administrative talent.”

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「若如君言，王公何以不任？」

translations.literal: Le said: “If like your words, why did the prince duke not employ them?”
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Prince Wang not employ him?"

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「王公由不能任，所以為明公擒也。」

translations.literal: Song said: “The prince duke because he could not employ them, therefore became the enlightened lord’s captive.”
translations.idiomatic: Song answered, “Because he could not use them, you captured him.”

sentences.zh: 勒方任之，裕乃微服潛遁。

translations.literal: Le was about to employ him; Yu then disguised himself and slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le meant to employ Yang Yu, who fled in disguise.

sentences.zh: 時鮮卑單于段眷為晉驃騎大將軍、遼西公，雅好人物，虛心延裕。

translations.literal: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of western Liaodong; by nature loved men of talent, humbly extended invitation to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Juan, Xianbei chieftain and Jin general, sought him eagerly.

sentences.zh: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！

translations.literal: Yu told friend Cheng Pan, saying: “Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi’s summons, used the gourd as metaphor; Yi Yin also said what affair is not lord, what people not subjects—even sages were thus; how much more our sort!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!

sentences.zh: 眷今召我，豈徒然哉！」

translations.literal: Juan now summons me—how could it be vain!”
translations.idiomatic: Duan Juan’s summons is no empty gesture!”

sentences.zh: 泮曰：「今華夏分崩，九州幅裂，軌跡所及，易水而已。

translations.literal: Pan said: “Now Huaxia split and crumbling, the nine provinces in tatters, where tracks reach is only to the Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pan replied, “China is shattered; beyond the Yi River there is no refuge.

sentences.zh: 欲偃蹇考槃，以待大通者，俟河之清也。

translations.literal: Desiring to recline and await the great penetration—waiting for the Yellow River to clear—is waiting for the river to clear.
translations.idiomatic: To hide and wait for peace is to wait for the Yellow River to run clear.

sentences.zh: 人壽幾何？

translations.literal: Human life how much?
translations.idiomatic: How long is a life?

sentences.zh: 古人以為白駒之歎。

translations.literal: The ancients took this as the white colt’s sigh.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients sighed at time’s white colt.

sentences.zh: 少遊有雲，郡掾足以廕後，況國相乎！

translations.literal: Shao You said, a commandery aide suffices to shade posterity—how much more a state chancellor!
translations.idiomatic: Even a county post can bless one’s heirs—let alone chancellor.

sentences.zh: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」

translations.literal: You trace Yi and Kong, or also know the moment’s spirit.”
translations.idiomatic: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”

sentences.zh: 裕乃應之。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon answered him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu accepted Duan Juan’s offer.

sentences.zh: 拜郎中令、中軍將軍，處上卿位。

translations.literal: Appointed Palace Director, Central Army General, occupying the upper minister’s seat.
translations.idiomatic: He was named palace director and central army general, ranking among the highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 曆事段氏五主，甚見尊重。

translations.literal: Passed through serving the Duan house’s five lords, greatly was respected.
translations.idiomatic: He served five successive Duan lords and won deep respect.

sentences.zh: 段遼與皝相攻，裕諫曰：「臣聞親仁善鄰，國之寶也。

translations.literal: Duan Liao and Huang attacked each other; Yu remonstrated, saying: “I have heard that cherishing benevolence and befriending neighbors is the state’s treasure.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Liao and Murong Huang clashed, Yang Yu urged, “A state’s greatest treasure is to cherish kindness and befriend one’s neighbors.

sentences.zh: 慕容與國世為婚姻，且皝令德之主，不宜連兵構怨，凋殘百姓。

translations.literal: Murong and the state generation after generation are marriage; moreover Huang is a lord of ordered virtue; ought not join arms and build resentment, withering the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The Murong house and yours have intermarried for generations; Murong Huang is a man of virtue—you must not exhaust the people in vendetta.

sentences.zh: 臣恐禍害之興，將由於此。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the rise of disaster and harm will stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: I fear calamity will come of this feud.

sentences.zh: 願兩追前失，通款如初，使國家有太山之安，蒼生蒙息肩之惠。」

translations.literal: Wish both pursue former faults, communicate sincerity as at the beginning, cause the state to have Mount Tai’s peace, the black-haired people to receive the favor of resting shoulders.”
translations.idiomatic: Let both sides forget old quarrels and restore peace so the realm stands firm as Taishan and the people can lay down their burdens.”

sentences.zh: 遼不從。

translations.literal: Liao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao refused.

sentences.zh: 出為燕郡太守。

translations.literal: Went out as Yan commandery grand warden.
translations.idiomatic: He left court to become grand warden of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 石季龍克令支，裕以郡降，拜北平太守，徵為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong took Lingzhi; Yu with the commandery surrendered; appointed Beiping grand warden; summoned as Left Assistant to the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu seized Lingzhi, Yang Yu surrendered his commandery, was named grand warden of Beiping, then recalled as left assistant in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 段遼之請迎于季龍也，裕以左丞領征東麻秋司馬。

translations.literal: At the time of Duan Liao’s request to welcome from Jilong, Yu as left assistant concurrently led Eastern Campaign Ma Qiu’s major.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Liao asked Shi Hu for an escort, Yang Yu served as chief clerk under Ma Qiu.

sentences.zh: 秋敗，裕為軍人所執，將詣皝。

translations.literal: When Qiu was defeated, Yu was seized by soldiers, was about to be brought to Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu’s defeat left Yang Yu a prisoner on his way to Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 皝素聞裕名，即命釋其囚，拜郎中令，遷大將軍左司馬。

translations.literal: Huang plain had heard Yu’s name; immediately ordered release his bonds; appointed Palace Director; promoted Grand General’s Left Major.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang, who had long admired him, freed him at once, named him palace director, then promoted him to senior major on his staff.

sentences.zh: 東破高句麗，北滅宇文歸，皆豫其謀，皝甚器重之。

translations.literal: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—both he pre-planned their strategies; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: He helped plan the eastern victory over Goguryeo and the northern destruction of Yuwen Gui, and Huang came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 及遷都和龍，裕雅有巧思，皝所制城池宮闔，皆裕之規模。

translations.literal: When moved the capital to Helong, Yu by nature had clever thought; the city walls and palace towers Huang regulated were all Yu’s models.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital shifted to Helong, Yang Yu’s engineering shaped every wall and tower Murong Huang built.

sentences.zh: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。

translations.literal: Although Yu served Huang daily nearer, favor and rank above the old men’s, nature humble and respectful, clear and frugal, firm, simple, kind, and earnest; although passed through dwelling at court’s apex, like a scholar in plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose above older favorites, he lived modestly and treated everyone like a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 士大夫流亡羈絕者，莫不經營收葬，存恤孤遺，士無賢不肖皆傾身待之，是以所在推仰。

translations.literal: Grandees and scholars who fled in exile and were cut off—none he did not arrange burial for, preserve and pity orphans left behind; gentry whether worthy or not all he inclined his person to treat; therefore wherever he was was pushed and looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: He buried exiles, aided their orphans, and honored every gentleman he met, winning universal esteem.

sentences.zh: 初，范陽盧諶每稱之曰：「吾及晉之清平，曆觀朝士多矣，忠清簡毅，篤信義烈，如陽士倫者，實亦未幾。」

translations.literal: In the beginning, Fan Yang’s Lu Chen always praised him, saying: “I have reached Jin’s clear peace, broadly viewed many court gentlemen; loyal, pure, concise, resolute, faithful in duty and fierce in righteousness—like Yang Shilun, in truth also not many.”
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chen of Fanyang once said, “In times of peace I have known many officials, but few match Yang Yu in loyalty, austerity, and steadfast faith.”

sentences.zh: 及死，皝甚悼之，時年六十二。

translations.literal: When he died, Huang greatly mourned him; at the time age sixty-two sui.
translations.idiomatic: When he died at sixty-two, Murong Huang mourned him deeply.
